notes: Split from G p21's Spanner row (see also RES-012, RES-079 and RES-080). Neither blueprint lists which actions are 'stricter', and the traceability work must name them. Transfers are live-capital actions and BLOCKED regardless (ADR 0021); the refusal can be verified in paper.

title: Outcomes accumulate durably in the Fabric while the ledger is down
statement: While the ledger is unavailable, outcome partitions accumulate durably in the Fabric under P1 retention, so that no financial outcome is lost.
rationale: The ledger outage must cost time, not outcomes. If outcomes aged out of the Fabric before the ledger returned, they would be lost for good.

sources.section: §22 Dependency Degradation Contracts — Spanner row, Platform behavior ('Outcome partitions accumulate durably in Fabric')

verification.check: Deny ledger writes for a period while trading continues. Assert that every outcome produced is retained in the Fabric's outcome partitions for at least the outage plus the catch-up time.

notes: G p22's ledger-outage game day calls this 'Fabric P1 retention'. LEDGER-033 (no outcome is dropped) is the ledger-side counterpart.

title: When the ledger is restored, the ledger writer replays outcomes idempotently
statement: When the ledger is restored, the ledger writer replays the accumulated outcomes idempotently, committing each exactly once in effect.
rationale: Catch-up after an outage is when duplicates are most likely, because the writer cannot know which commits landed just before the failure. Idempotency by event_id is what keeps the recovery from corrupting the books.

sources.section: §22 Dependency Degradation Contracts — Spanner row, Platform behavior ('ledger writer replays idempotently when restored')

verification.check: Restore ledger writes after an outage and replay the backlog twice. Assert that each outcome's event_id is committed exactly once and that balances match an outage-free run.

notes: LEDGER-020 (exactly once in effect, by event_id) is the mechanism, and this requirement is its recovery case.

title: Loss of Bigtable or BigQuery has no direct impact on the hot path
statement: Loss of Bigtable or BigQuery has no direct impact on the Reflex hot path. Only research, replay and features degrade.
rationale: Analytical and feature stores are reached asynchronously. If their loss could touch the hot path, a synchronous dependency would have crept in.

sources.section: §22 Dependency Degradation Contracts — Bigtable/BigQuery row ('No direct hot impact'; 'Research/replay/features degrade')

verification.check: Make both stores unreachable. Assert that reflex decision latency and fill rate are unchanged, while research and feature jobs report a degraded state.

notes: Split from G p21's Bigtable/BigQuery row (RES-082). The stores are in ADR 0099 conflict C4. P1 as GCP Phase 5 (data plane).

title: Fabric and GCS preserve the source history that derived stores are rebuilt from
statement: When Bigtable or BigQuery is lost, the Fabric and GCS still hold the source history, so that the derived stores can be rebuilt from it.
rationale: A derived store that holds the only copy of its history is not derived. Losing it would lose the history.

sources.section: §22 Dependency Degradation Contracts — Bigtable/BigQuery row, Platform behavior ('Fabric/GCS preserve source history')

verification.check: Drop a derived table, rebuild it from the Fabric and GCS history, and assert that the rebuilt table matches the original.

notes: DATA-066 states the rebuild.

title: Research queues as a backlog while the AI/Agent Platform is down
statement: When the AI/Agent Platform is unavailable, research work queues as a backlog and is processed when the platform returns, rather than being dropped.
rationale: Research requests raised during an outage are often about the very conditions that caused it. Dropping them loses the questions the platform most needs answered.

sources.section: §22 Dependency Degradation Contracts — AI/Agent Platform row, Platform behavior ('research backlog queues')

verification.check: Submit research tasks during an AI-platform outage. Assert that each is durably queued and that each is processed exactly once after recovery.

notes: Split from G p21's AI/Agent Platform row. The row's Reflex half ('no new cognitive/model output', 'existing packages continue') is in RES-005. NON_RUST was dropped because queueing research tasks needs nothing outside Rust. MANAGED_SERVICE is kept because the dependency named is Agent Platform/Vertex (ADR 0099 C4 and C5). P1 as master Phase 2 (cognitive data loop).

title: Strategies that depend on a lost venue feed stop
statement: When a venue market-data feed is lost, the strategies that depend on that feed stop.
rationale: A strategy acting on a stale feed trades against prices that no longer exist.

sources.section: §22 Dependency Degradation Contracts — Market data venue feed row, Reflex behavior ('Stop strategies dependent on stale feed')

verification.check: Stall a simulated feed. Assert that every strategy consuming it stops placing orders once the feed's staleness threshold is crossed, and that strategies on other feeds continue.

notes: Split from G p21's venue-feed row (RES-084 to RES-086). LIVE_CAPITAL was dropped: stopping a strategy, and hedging or exiting against the simulated venue, can all be verified in paper (ADR 0003).

title: Exposure left by a lost venue feed is hedged or exited by a local playbook
statement: When a venue feed is lost, open exposure that depended on it is hedged or exited according to a local playbook.
rationale: Stopping new orders leaves the existing position exposed to prices the platform can no longer see. A local playbook acts on that without waiting for a centre that may be unreachable too.

sources.section: §22 Dependency Degradation Contracts — Market data venue feed row, Reflex behavior ('hedge/exit according to local playbook')

verification.check: Stall a feed while a position is open. Assert that the cell executes its local playbook's hedge or exit, recorded with the playbook's version.

notes: Split from G p21's venue-feed row. LIVE_CAPITAL was dropped for the reason given in RES-084.

title: A lost venue feed journals incident and reconciliation events
statement: A venue-feed loss produces incident and reconciliation events in the journal.
rationale: The actions taken during a feed outage have to be explained afterwards. Without the journaled incident, the hedge looks like an unexplained trade.

sources.section: §22 Dependency Degradation Contracts — Market data venue feed row, Platform behavior ('Incident and reconciliation events journaled')

verification.check: Stall a feed. Assert that an incident event is journaled for it and, after recovery, a reconciliation event.

notes: Split from G p21's venue-feed row. LIVE_CAPITAL was dropped for the reason given in RES-084.

title: Losing GitHub or GitOps leaves the running system unchanged
statement: Loss of GitHub or GitOps leaves the running system unchanged. Only new deployments stop.
rationale: The source of truth for change is not a runtime dependency. If an outage at a code host could restart or roll back production, the delivery pipeline would itself be a failure mode.

sources.section: §22 Dependency Degradation Contracts — GitHub/GitOps row ('Running system unchanged'; 'No new deployments')

verification.check: Block the platform's access to GitHub and to the GitOps controller. Assert that every running workload keeps serving, that no workload is restarted or rolled back, and that no deployment proceeds.

notes: Split from G p21's GitHub/GitOps row (RES-087 and RES-088). CICD-073 states the same for the GitOps management plane. KUBERNETES is kept because v2.1's GitOps tooling runs on Kubernetes (ADR 0099 C3; ADR 0093 suspended the control-plane cluster). P0 as a supply-chain invariant (GCP Phase 1).

title: Emergency change without GitOps uses only a pre-approved break-glass runbook, reconciled to Git afterwards
statement: While GitHub or GitOps is unavailable, emergency change uses only a pre-approved break-glass runbook, and every break-glass change is reconciled into Git afterwards.
rationale: An emergency with no approved path invites improvised console changes that nobody records. Reconciling to Git afterwards is what stops the emergency fix from becoming permanent, undocumented drift.

sources.section: §22 Dependency Degradation Contracts — GitHub/GitOps row, Platform behavior ('emergency runbook uses pre-approved break-glass process with later reconciliation to Git')

verification.check: Exercise the break-glass runbook in a nonprod environment. Assert that the change was made only through the runbook's pre-approved steps, and that Git holds a matching commit afterwards with no drift left.

notes: Break-glass cannot relax the paper-trading boundary or deploy to prod. Prod stays refused by infra.yml and the deploy gate, and needs a human dispatch. G p23 §28 forbids undocumented emergency config (CICD-004). P1 because this is an operational runbook, not a foundation exit test.

title: Quarterly regional-loss game day
statement: A regional-loss game day runs every quarter. One execution region is removed from service and control networking, and the exercise verifies three things: the other regions continue, mirrors and recovery behave, and no cross-region arbitrage assumes the missing peer.
rationale: Regional independence that has never been exercised is an assumption. The first real regional outage is the worst time to learn which cycle quietly depended on the lost peer.

sources.section: §25 Resilience Testing and Game Days — Quarterly regional-loss game day bullet

verification.check: Check each quarter's record for the region removed and for evidence of each of the three verifications: continuation, mirror and recovery behaviour, and no cycle naming the missing peer.

notes: Exercises RES-007, RES-008 and RES-063 to RES-067. It runs in staging, the environment G p21 §24 assigns to failure and game-day validation; prod is refused. It needs more than one deployed region (ADR 0099 C8).

title: Monthly zonal-failure game day
statement: A zonal-failure game day runs every month. A Reflex primary, or the Fabric replicas in one zone, are terminated, and the exercise proves fencing, quorum, failover and bounded outcome loss.
rationale: Zonal failures are the most frequent infrastructure fault. A failover path that runs only when one happens is a path nobody has seen work.

sources.section: §25 Resilience Testing and Game Days — Monthly zonal failure bullet

verification.check: Check each month's record for the component terminated, the fencing and quorum evidence, the failover time, and the measured outcome loss against its bound.

notes: Exercises RES-057 to RES-059 and RES-068. NEW_DEPENDENCY is kept as extracted: the v2.1 Fabric this exercises rests on dependency classes that ADR 0099 C2 has not yet decided (consensus and transport). The CI form of the same fault test belongs to the Fabric MVP exit test (ARCH-063, 'chaos tests before application adoption'), which is P0.

title: Broker-backpressure game day
statement: A broker-backpressure game day freezes a sink and fills consumer lag, and verifies that priority QoS holds and that broker memory does not explode.
rationale: Backpressure is where a broker either sheds the right traffic or collapses under all of it. The difference shows only under load.

sources.section: §25 Resilience Testing and Game Days — Broker backpressure bullet

verification.check: Check the record shows that higher-priority classes kept their latency and delivery while the frozen sink's lag grew, and that broker memory stayed within its limit.

notes: M p36 §26.1 requires explicit per-stream quotas, lag limits and an overload policy; this game day exercises them. NEW_DEPENDENCY is kept for the same reason as RES-090.

title: Ledger-outage game day
statement: A ledger-outage game day denies Spanner writes and verifies Fabric P1 retention, the degradation of local capital freshness, and then idempotent catch-up.
rationale: The ledger path is the one where a recovery bug turns directly into wrong money. It has to be exercised, not only designed.

sources.section: §25 Resilience Testing and Game Days — Ledger outage bullet

verification.check: Check the record shows the outcomes retained during the denial, the cells narrowing as their capital freshness decayed, and every outcome committed exactly once after writes returned.

notes: Exercises RES-012, RES-079 and RES-080. Spanner is in ADR 0099 conflict C4.

title: Bad model or package game day
statement: A bad-model/package game day promotes an intentionally degraded candidate in nonprod or staging, and verifies that the shadow, replay or SLO gate blocks it or rolls it back.
rationale: A promotion gate that has never been shown a bad candidate has not been shown to work.

sources.section: §25 Resilience Testing and Game Days — Bad model/package bullet

verification.check: Check the record shows that the degraded candidate never reached authority, or was rolled back, and which gate caught it.

notes: NON_RUST is kept because v2.1's model packages come from the Python training stack (ADR 0099 C5). P1 as master Phase 2 (model/strategy foundry).

title: Bad schema game day
statement: A bad-schema game day attempts an incompatible Fabric schema change. The CI or runtime schema registry must reject it before any production consumer breaks.
rationale: An incompatible schema that reaches consumers breaks every one of them at once, and the records written under it cannot be read back for replay.

sources.section: §25 Resilience Testing and Game Days — Bad schema bullet

verification.check: Check the record shows that the incompatible schema was rejected at CI or at registry admission, and that no consumer saw a record written under it.

notes: CICD-069 requires the versioned registry. NEW_DEPENDENCY is kept because v2.1's schema is Protobuf via prost (ADR 0099 C2).

title: Agent-compromise simulation game day
statement: An agent-compromise game day gives an autonomous development agent malicious instructions or input, and verifies that the secret, network, merge and prod-deploy boundaries prevent any escalation of authority.
rationale: Agent boundaries are written on the assumption that the agent is honest. Only a simulated compromise shows whether they hold when it is not.

sources.section: §25 Resilience Testing and Game Days — Agent compromise simulation bullet

verification.check: Check the record shows that each of the four boundaries was attempted and held: no secret was read, no unapproved egress was made, nothing was merged without review, and nothing was deployed to prod.

notes: The boundaries it tests are GOV-026 to GOV-028. This repository already runs agents under a guard hook and settings that deny reads of key material and block destructive commands (01-security-and-safety.md). This game day would test those boundaries. P2 as GCP Phase 9 (autonomous development).

title: A regional GKE cluster is rebuilt from zero
statement: A regional GKE cluster is periodically rebuilt from zero using only Terraform, Git and artifacts, proving that it has no undocumented console dependency.
rationale: Infrastructure that has only ever been modified, and never recreated, accumulates hand-made state nobody knows about until it has to be rebuilt in an emergency.

sources.section: §25 Resilience Testing and Game Days — Rebuild from zero bullet ('rebuild a regional GKE cluster')

verification.check: Check the record shows the cluster destroyed and recreated from the committed Terraform and Git state with no manual console step, and the workloads it served healthy again.

notes: Split from G p22's rebuild bullet; the Fabric half is RES-097. GCP-048 states the same. MULTI_REGION was dropped because only one regional cluster is rebuilt. This pass added COST because the rebuild creates billable infrastructure (ADR 0093). ADR 0099 C3 applies, and the Cloud Run equivalent is rebuilding a region's services from Terraform. Destroying the cluster deletes resources, which needs explicit approval in the conversation (02-change-management.md).

title: A nonprod Fabric cluster is rebuilt from zero
statement: A nonprod Fabric cluster is periodically rebuilt from zero using only Terraform, Git and artifacts, proving that it has no undocumented console dependency.
rationale: The Fabric holds the platform's event history. A Fabric that cannot be recreated from code cannot be recovered with confidence after a real loss.

sources.section: §25 Resilience Testing and Game Days — Rebuild from zero bullet ('and a nonprod Fabric cluster')

verification.check: Check the record shows a nonprod Fabric cluster recreated from committed Terraform and artifacts alone, and passing its conformance tests afterwards.

notes: Split from RES-096. KUBERNETES, MANAGED_SERVICE and MULTI_REGION were dropped: the Fabric runs on its own VMs in its own project (G p4 prod/fabric-<region>), not on GKE or a managed service, and the rebuild covers one cluster. This pass added COST (ADR 0093).

title: Every critical component is exercised in scheduled game days
statement: Every critical component is exercised in scheduled game days.
rationale: A component left out of the schedule is exactly the one whose failure mode nobody has seen.

sources.section: §27 Architecture Acceptance Criteria ('Every critical component is exercised in scheduled game days')

verification.check: Compare the declared list of critical components against the game-day schedule and records. Assert that each component has been exercised within its scheduled period.

notes: Split from the G p23 acceptance item; the RTO/RPO half is RES-099. Neither blueprint gives the list of critical components, and it must be declared before this can be checked.

title: Every critical component has an observable RTO and RPO, or a documented reason why not
statement: Every critical component has an observable recovery time objective (RTO) and recovery point objective (RPO), or a documented reason why exact guarantees cannot be promised.
rationale: An RTO nobody measures is a hope. Where a guarantee genuinely cannot be given, saying so in writing is more useful than an unmeasured number.

sources.section: §27 Architecture Acceptance Criteria ('has observable RTO/RPO or a documented reason exact guarantees cannot be promised')

verification.check: For each declared critical component, assert that it has either an RTO and RPO together with a metric or game-day measurement of each, or a written reason, and that no component has neither.

notes: 'Observable' means measured in operation or in a game day, not only declared. The observability rules forbid describing the platform as observable until scraping is proven, so today most of these figures can only be declared.
